svg.title: Storage near and far from H100 execution units
svg.desc: Registers, shared memory and L1, L2, and HBM differ in capacity, scope, and who manages them. These are storage choices, not a required path for every load.
svg.text: Where does the working data live?
H100 example. Capacity, access latency, and bandwidth are different properties.
Private values for each thread, including partial sums
Shared memory: the block's program-managed working space
L1: hardware-managed cached data near the execution units
Cached data shared across the GPU's SMs
Large off-chip memory holding inputs and outputs
Near storage is smaller. Retain useful data there to reduce repeated transfers.
Global loads do not automatically stage data in shared memory.
